comment: Provisional. Ratios from 3 runs on 2026-11-16, load average 200 to 229 on a shared 512-core machine: keyed yuka/solid 1.058, 1.144 and 1.152 (the last from make bench-gate); ssr yuka-stream/solid-node 1.389, 1.603 and 1.368; LCP page/plain HTML 1.04 to 1.64; TBT 0 ms on every page. The server-reason-react limit is from bench/ssr/README.md (1.76 after ticket 31), since it is out of the build. max_js_raw is the exact raw bytes of JavaScript files and inline scripts of each page: change it with the change that changes the bytes. Set again on 5349ba5: pull requests 27, 28 and 30 grew / and /my to 200,388 B and /issue/YUK-1 to 170,568 B without a change here, and pull request 26 then moved the router code out of the start chunk. Raised by 830 B on each page for issue 11: the scheduler walks a chain of memos with a loop. Raised by 199 B on /, /my and /issue/YUK-1 for Action.start, the abort of a query Action.call when its owner is disposed, and a form answer that arrives after its form is gone. Raised by 141 B on /, /my and /issue/YUK-1 for the demo issue overlay: c21860e (close on a click outside, Close button in the page header) added 157 B without a change here, and 0dbb27d removed 16 B. SSR solid-node limit set to 1.0 (the v1 target, SSR faster than Solid) from 20 main CI runs on ubuntu-latest, 2026-11-16. The rounds of one run agree: per-round yuka-stream/solid-node ratios differ by 4.4% or less in a run. The runs do not: the ratio groups by runner, seen in the absolute req/s of solid-node. Solid near 3,800 to 4,250 req/s: 8 runs, 1.229 to 1.268. Near 5,250 to 5,550: 7 runs, 1.202 to 1.262. Near 6,700 to 7,000: 3 runs, 1.062, 1.104 and 1.122 (5ca0734, 6d21a08, 3f156ec; 6d21a08 changes only docs after f6a3ce7 at 1.252). Near 7,100 to 7,300: 2 runs, 1.283 and 1.313. Both servers use one thread, so the groups come from the runner CPU type; more or paired rounds do not change them (paired-round medians move each run by 0.025 or less). With 1.0 all 20 runs pass and the worst keeps a margin of 5.9%. The Yuka slowdown that fails a run is 5.9% to 10.8% on the slowest group and 16.8% to 23.9% on the others: replayed on the 20 runs, a 10% slowdown fails 2 and a 20% slowdown fails 11. A tighter limit needs a limit per CPU: run.ts records the CPU model in the result and the log, so collect it first. Raised for compiled-view step 1 (each child and attribute of an HTML tag that is not a constant is a hole): / and /my by 74 B, /issue/YUK-1 by 79 B. The bytes are calls of functions of other modules in the markup, which are now holes: the hrefs from Links, Theme.label and the Model.Issue labels. Raised by 5 B on / and /my and lowered by 4 B on /issue/YUK-1 for Remote.state and Live.state: each Remote.make and Live.make keeps a memo of the status with the optimistic changes applied, made in one helper of Optimistic for both. Raised by 88 B on /, /my and /issue/YUK-1 for the runtime part of the static-hole drop: an effect, hole or attribute hole whose first run reads no State is not kept by its owner, unless it adds a bubbling event handler, whose owner must be disposed with its parent. The JavaScript heap of /w/stress (2,000 rows) goes from 14.60 to 11.86 MB (11.16 MB before every non-constant JSX expression was a hole; 11.17 MB when a handler did not keep its owner). The server part (no markers for such a hole) was not kept: it cost 543 B more on / and /my, 487 B more on /issue/YUK-1 and 0.23 MB more heap on /w/stress, for 30 fewer comment nodes on /insights. Raised by 203 B on /, /my and /issue/YUK-1 for State.select: a read of a memo first updates a selector whose source changed, so a memo over is_selected is up to date in a batch. Set to the measured bytes for Async.memo (ticket 15): main measured 192,049 B on / and /my and 161,108 B on /issue/YUK-1, under the old limits; Async.memo makes them 192,845 B (+796) and 161,876 B (+768). The bytes are the source protocol that Remote now uses (the boundary binding in the owner env and its lookup), placed in the start chunk because async.js imports it, and the check in a query Action.call for an answer in the page. Raised for Yuka.Pending (ticket 16), measured against 39ea93d on the same machine: / and /my from 192,845 to 193,696 B (+851), /issue/YUK-1 from 161,876 to 162,667 B (+791). On /: the island registry entry of the new demo page /pending (+129 B in main.js); a 457 B chunk that esbuild splits out of a 6,177 B chunk (-416 B there) for code that the lazy /pending island shares with the start code; +390 B in the main shared chunk for the mount functions that client.js gives to the Pending code, Await with an optional loading and the default of Async.waiter; and +281 B in four other shared chunks, mostly the boundary join of a Remote.make on the server and minified names. The Pending code itself (boundary.js, pending_dom.js) is only in the chunk of the /pending island. Set again for the live old view of a held hole: / and /my -12 B, /issue/YUK-1 +18 B. The change is only in pending_dom.js; the modules of the start code have the same bytes in the esbuild output, and the difference is the names that the minifier gives. Lowered by 45 B on /, /my and /issue/YUK-1 for ticket 52 (the first run of Async.memo waits for an answer that the server still streams): the answer reader of Async.memo now calls the transport itself, so the query Action.call in client.js only picks the reader or the transport. The wait code is in embedded.js, used only by Async.memo.
